docs.title: kDomainBench
docs.text:
kDomainBench benchmarks ten methods that estimate the number of spatial domains (k) in spatial transcriptomics data. The kdomainbench package runs each method from Python and compares its estimated k with the number of domains in a manual reference annotation. It is for researchers who want to estimate k for their own 10x Visium samples, or to compare k-estimation methods. 

import kdomainbench as kdb
clusters = kdb.run("SpaGCN", "sample.h5ad")

Get started How it works

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: The package is imported as import kdomainbench as kdb. Its functions form four groups (methods, run, scores, figures) plus setup. Each name links to its reference entry, with the parameters and examples.

docs.title: 1. Methods
docs.text:
call returns kdb.list_methods(gpu_only=) The method names. gpu_only=True keeps the three with GPU code. kdb.get_method(name) One method's settings: language, environment, GPU, use of kmax. kdb.Method The record get_method returns. kdb.METHODS Every method's record, by name. 
import kdomainbench as kdb
kdb.list_methods(gpu_only=True)          # ['CellCharter', 'DeepST', 'SpatialDE2']
kdb.get_method("DR.SC").uses_kmax        # True

docs.title: 2. Run
docs.text:
call returns kdb.run(method, h5ad, kmax=, device=, out_root=, gpu_id=) The domain of each spot. The run folder keeps the log and run_info.json. kdb.run_all(h5ad, kmax=, device=, methods=, out_root=, gpu_id=) Method name → domains, for every method that succeeded. kdb.MethodFailed Raised by run when a method stops with an error or writes no labels. 
h5ad = "data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad"
clusters = kdb.run("SpaGCN", h5ad, kmax=30, device="cpu")
results = kdb.run_all(h5ad, kmax=30, device="gpu", gpu_id=0, out_root="kdb_results_gpu")

docs.title: 3. Scores
docs.text:
call returns kdb.read_clusters(path) The domains of one run folder. kdb.reference_annotation(h5ad, reference_key=) The annotated domain of each spot. kdb.evaluate(clusters, reference) k_estimated, k_reference, k_error, ARI, NMI, n_spots_scored. kdb.metrics(run, h5ad=, recompute=) The twelve metrics of the paper for one run, saved as metric.csv. kdb.MetricsFailed Raised by metrics when the metric code stops. kdb.load_results(root, reference_key=, score=, h5ad=) One row per run under root, scored. kdb.k_accuracy(summary) One row per method: mean |k error|, exact-k rate, mean ARI. 
kdb.evaluate("kdb_results/SpaGCN/D3_151509_5k_cpu", h5ad)
summary = kdb.load_results("kdb_results")
kdb.k_accuracy(summary)

docs.title: 4. Figures
docs.text:
call returns kdb.pl.plot_k_estimates(summary, k_reference=) Estimated k per method, the reference k dashed. kdb.pl.plot_metrics(summary) The metrics per method as a matrix of bars. kdb.pl.plot_runtime(summary, metric=) Run time or peak memory per method, CPU vs GPU. kdb.pl.plot_spatial(clusters, h5ad, legend=) One run's domains on the tissue. kdb.pl.plot_spatial_grid(results, h5ad) Several runs' domains in a grid. 
kdb.pl.plot_k_estimates(summary).figure.savefig("k.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
kdb.pl.plot_spatial_grid(results, h5ad, ncols=5).savefig("domains.png")

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Changes that users of kdomainbench notice, newest first. The format follows Keep a Changelog.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• kdb.metrics and kdomainbench metrics: the twelve metrics of the paper, computed by the paper's own metrics.R and scs.py. kdomainbench check --metrics tests them, and Rscript envs/install_r_packages.R --metrics installs their R packages.
  • A run folder records the package version and the settings that change a method (run_info.json fields kdomainbench and env), and the packages of the method's environment (packages.txt).
  • kdb.run_all ends with one warning that names every method that did not finish.
  • load_results(h5ad=) and kdomainbench summarize --h5ad score runs made on another machine. On the command line each file scores the runs of the dataset of its name, and --h5ad can be repeated. summarize --reference-key scores against another obs column.
  • kdb.pl.plot_metrics: the metrics of every run as a matrix of bars, laid out as Fig. 2f of the paper.
  • kdomainbench --version.
  • kdb.evaluate, kdb.reference_annotation and the plots accept an AnnData object for the input file and a run folder for the labels. kdb.evaluate also compares two runs.
  • kdomainbench check looks for every R package the method scripts load and reads an .h5ad file from R. check --gpu fails when no GPU is visible.
  • Pages: the how-to guides Your own data, Run on a cluster and Troubleshooting, the Command line reference, FAQ, Citation, Contributing and Changelog.
  • CONTRIBUTING.md, and a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the tests and builds the site.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Breaking: kdb.run takes out_root instead of out_dir, with the folder layout of kdb.run_all and kdomainbench run -o: <out_root>/<method>/<dataset>_<device>.
  • Breaking, to the terms of the paper: ground_truth is now reference_annotation (its key is reference_key), k_true is k_reference, truth_key is reference_key, evaluate(truth=) is evaluate(reference=), and the n_spots of evaluate is n_spots_scored. plot_k_estimates(k_true=) is plot_k_estimates(k_reference=).
  • kdb.pl.plot_k_estimates has one row per method and colors each dot by its distance from the reference k, as Fig. 2b of the paper. Runs of several datasets are drawn as k errors. Breaking: k_reference takes one number, not a list.
  • gpu_id defaults to the GPUs a scheduler names in CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, else GPU 0.
  • kmax is checked before any method starts: at least 2, and at most 30 for BNPSpace.
  • A run that is stopped or fails stays on record with "success": false, and labels or metrics of an earlier run in the same folder are deleted first.
  • load_results raises FileNotFoundError for a folder that does not exist and always returns the score columns. It raises ValueError when one h5ad file is given for runs of several datasets.
  • kdb.run and kdb.run_all stop before any method starts when the input is a folder or not an .h5ad file.
  • kdomainbench summarize prints the main columns, and each reason a run was not scored once. --csv keeps every column. Warnings print without Python's source line.
  • kdomainbench run, metrics and summarize exit with an error code when a method did not finish, a metric could not be computed or no run succeeded.
  • A fatal error of kdomainbench is one line that starts with kdomainbench: error:, and a method named twice runs once.
  • kdb.read_clusters, kdb.load_results(h5ad=), kdb.k_accuracy and the plots say what is wrong with their input: a run that did not finish, an input file that does not exist, a table without the columns of load_results.
  • kdb.pl.plot_spatial_grid titles each map <method> (k = n).
  • drsc.R no longer reads obs["clusters"], so it runs on files without an annotation.
  • Python 3.10 or later.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• The docs extra of pyproject.toml. Use docs/requirements.txt.
  • cowplot from envs/install_r_packages.R: no method script loads it.
First version: ten methods behind kdb.run, kdb.run_all and kdomainbench run, scoring with kdb.evaluate, kdb.load_results and kdb.k_accuracy, and the plots in kdb.pl.

docs.title: Reporting a run
docs.text: To make a result reproducible, report the package version and commit, kmax and the device. The run folder records the rest: run_info.json holds the exact call of the method script (command) and the settings that change a method (env), and packages.txt the package versions of its environment.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Questions, bug reports and changes are welcome as issues and pull requests on GitHub: https://github.com/PYangLab/domainNumber/issues.

docs.title: Ask a question or report a bug
docs.text:
Open an issue. For a run that failed or gave an unexpected result, attach:

  • the output of kdomainbench check,
  • run_info.json, packages.txt and the last 50 lines of run.log from the run folder,
  • the operating system, and whether the run used a GPU.

docs.title: Make a change
docs.text:
Set up a development copy in the cloned folder. The package needs Python 3.10 or later, and the site tools in docs/requirements.txt need Python 3.11 or later:

python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e . pytest -r docs/requirements.txt

Run the two checks before you open a pull request. They need no method environment and also run on macOS:

python -m pytest                  # the unit tests
mkdocs build --strict             # the site builds, and every link and anchor resolves

Two more checks need more than a laptop:

  • KDB_TEST_METRICS=1 python -m pytest tests/test_metrics.py computes the twelve metrics and compares them with the paper's values. It needs the metric R packages and kdb_py, and takes about 4 minutes.
  • python scripts/check_docs.py --h5ad data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad --reuse <finished runs> --work <scratch folder> runs the code examples of the pages it lists and of the docstrings (not the home page, and not the docstring example of kdb.metrics, which the first check covers). It needs Linux with the environments and takes about an hour. It checks that each example runs, not that it prints the output the page shows.

Add a line to CHANGELOG.md, under "Unreleased", for every change a user notices.

docs.title: Rules of the repository
docs.text:
• The method scripts (src/kdomainbench/methods/) and the metric scripts (src/kdomainbench/metric_scripts/) are copies of the scripts behind the paper. Change one only to fix a bug, describe the change under "Method scripts" in docs/overview.md, and update its checksum in tests/test_basic.py (METHOD_SCRIPTS) or tests/test_metrics.py (PAPER_SCRIPTS).
  • Some files are made by a script. Change the script and run it again, not the file:
File Made by snippets/results_table.md, and summary_5k.csv and the figures of the benchmark in docs/assets/ scripts/make_results_page.py envs/kdb_py.yml, envs/kdb_spatialde.yml envs/finalize_yml.py envs/kdb_r.lock.csv envs/export_r_lock.R docs/assets/logo.svg, docs/assets/favicon.svg scripts/make_logo.py
  • The words of the site: "reference annotation" and "reference domain number" (or reference k), never "ground truth" or "true k". Sentences are short and plain.

docs.title: Add a method
docs.text:
A method is one script in src/kdomainbench/methods/ and one Method(...) entry in src/kdomainbench/registry.py. The entry names the script, its environment (r, py or spatialde) and argv, the function that turns the input file, the run folder and kmax into the script's arguments. The script runs in the run folder and writes cluster_results.csv there, with the spot barcodes in the first column and the domain labels in a column named cluster.

Add its checksum to METHOD_SCRIPTS in tests/test_basic.py, its packages to envs/install_r_packages.R or the environment files, and its row to "The ten methods" in docs/overview.md and to the methods table of docs/citation.md.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Error messages and their fixes are under Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Do I need a GPU?
docs.text: No. All ten methods run on a CPU. CellCharter, DeepST and SpatialDE2 can also use a GPU (GPU or CPU?).

docs.title: My sample has no annotation. Can I still use kDomainBench?
docs.text: Yes. Every method still returns its domains and its estimated k. Only the scores need an annotation. Your own data walks through it.

docs.title: The methods give different k. Which one is right?
docs.text: No single run tells you. The methods will disagree says how to read their estimates.

docs.title: Does it work for mouse, or for another tissue?
docs.text: Yes. No method takes the species or the tissue as a setting. Each reads only the count matrix and the spot coordinates of a 10x Visium sample. The results on this site are from human brain samples of one study.

docs.title: Can I use Jupyter?
docs.text:
Yes, with kdb_py as the kernel. kdb_py has no Jupyter server, so use the Jupyter of the Linux machine where the methods run (JupyterLab, JupyterHub or Open OnDemand). Register kdb_py with it once, then pick it as the kernel:

terminal
conda run -n kdb_py python -m ipykernel install --user --name kdb_py

For environments made with KDB_ENVS_DIR, name kdb_py by its path: conda run -p /project/envs/kdb_py ....

When Jupyter does not see the R on your PATH, name it at the top of the notebook with kdb.set_env("r", "/path/to/Rscript").

docs.title: Can I score labels from another tool?
docs.text:
Yes. kdb.evaluate takes any labels indexed by spot barcode:

import pandas as pd
import kdomainbench as kdb

labels = pd.read_csv("my_labels.csv", index_col=0).iloc[:, 0]      # barcode, label
kdb.evaluate(labels, "data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad")

n_spots_scored in the result must equal your number of spots. A smaller number means that some barcodes did not match.

docs.title: Can I add a method?
docs.text: Yes, as a script and one entry in the package. Contributing says what the script receives and must write.

docs.title: How do I run on a cluster?
docs.text: Run on a cluster installs the environments in a project folder and submits one job per method.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
kdomainbench is a Python package, installed into the kdb_py conda environment. The ten methods run in three environments: two conda environments for the Python methods and your own R for the R methods. kDomainBench starts each method in the right one.

You need For Linux (x86-64) running the methods. The environments are built for it conda or mamba (Miniforge) the two Python environments, about 12 GB of disk A C++ compiler, cmake and git building louvain for SpaGCN, fetching SpatialDE2, and the R packages R ≥ 4.4 the six R methods. The four Python methods run without it R ≥ 4.5 with Bioconductor ≥ 3.22 (optional) the twelve metrics of the paper (The metric packages) An NVIDIA GPU with driver ≥ 525 (optional) CellCharter, DeepST and SpatialDE2 can use one. The GPU libraries come with the environments

macOS and Windows

The methods run on Linux only. Scoring and plotting finished runs works on any system with Python 3.10 or later. In the cloned folder:

python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install --upgrade pip && .venv/bin/pip install -e .

Summary

git clone https://github.com/PYangLab/domainNumber.git && cd domainNumber
bash envs/install_envs.sh                 # the two Python environments
Rscript envs/install_r_packages.R         # the R packages, into your R
conda activate kdb_py
kdomainbench check                        # checks that every environment starts

docs.title: Step 1: Get the code
docs.text:
terminal
git clone https://github.com/PYangLab/domainNumber.git
cd domainNumber

The repository holds the package (src/kdomainbench/), one script per method (src/kdomainbench/methods/), the environment files (envs/) and the example file (data/, see Example data).

Private repository

The repository is private. git clone asks for your GitHub login and works only for members. Use a personal access token as the password, or clone over SSH (git@github.com:PYangLab/domainNumber.git).

docs.title: The Python environments
docs.text:
terminal
bash envs/install_envs.sh

This creates the conda environments kdb_py and kdb_spatialde, with the package versions fixed in envs/, and installs the kdomainbench package into kdb_py. The same environments run on machines with and without a GPU.

KDB_ENVS_DIR=/project/envs bash envs/install_envs.sh creates them in that folder instead of conda's default one. Activate kdb_py then by its path: conda activate /project/envs/kdb_py.

docs.title: R
docs.text:
The R methods use the R you already have (R ≥ 4.4, with Bioconductor 3.19 or later). Install the packages the methods need:

terminal
Rscript envs/install_r_packages.R

The script installs only what is missing, from CRAN and Bioconductor, at their current versions. It installs into R's main library, or into your personal library when the main one is read-only, as with an R from a module.

Source Packages CRAN PRECAST, DR.SC, iSC.MEB, Seurat, Rcpp, RcppArmadillo, flexclust, philentropy, fastcluster, dynamicTreeCut, purrr, deldir, glue, ggplot2, mclust (plus remotes and BiocManager to install the rest) Bioconductor BayesSpace, zellkonverter, SingleCellExperiment, SummarizedExperiment, scran, scater, scuttle, BiocSingular CRAN archive SC.MEB 1.1 (no longer on CRAN)

BNPSpace is not a package. Its C++ code ships with kDomainBench and is compiled at the start of each run.

A separate R library

To keep these packages apart from your other R work, give the script a folder and tell kDomainBench about it. The R methods then see only this library and base R.

terminal
Rscript envs/install_r_packages.R /project/kdb_rlib
export KDB_R_LIB=/project/kdb_rlib

docs.text:
This step is optional. kdb.evaluate scores a run with k error, ARI and NMI and needs nothing more. The twelve metrics of the paper (Evaluate a run) are computed by the paper's own code, whose R part needs these packages:

Source Packages CRAN clevr, aricode, ClusterR Bioconductor spARI, zellkonverter, SummarizedExperiment, HDF5Array, rhdf5 GitHub, at the commits used for the paper lisi, SPARK, SpatialPCA

spARI is in Bioconductor from release 3.22, which needs R ≥ 4.5. The command that installs them depends on your R:

Your R (Rscript -e 'BiocManager::version()' gives the Bioconductor release) What to do R ≥ 4.5 on Bioconductor ≥ 3.22 Rscript envs/install_r_packages.R --metrics. With a separate library, add its folder: Rscript envs/install_r_packages.R --metrics $KDB_R_LIB R ≥ 4.5 on Bioconductor 3.21 update Bioconductor first: Rscript -e 'BiocManager::install(version = "3.22")' R 4.4 or older install R ≥ 4.5 next to it and run /path/to/R-4.5/bin/Rscript envs/install_r_packages.R --metrics, then export KDB_METRICS_RSCRIPT=/path/to/R-4.5/bin/Rscript

kdomainbench check --metrics computes the twelve metrics on a small test sample.

docs.title: Example data
docs.text:
The tutorials use the DLPFC Visium sample 151509 from the spatialLIBD study (Maynard et al., Nature Neuroscience 2021 and spatialLIBD). Each spot carries the study's manual annotation of six cortical layers (Layer1–Layer6) and white matter (WM). This is the reference annotation. It has 7 domains, so the reference domain number is k = 7.

The file comes with the code as data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad (14 MB): D3 is the number of the dataset in the benchmark, and 5k its rounded number of spots. It is the benchmark's copy of the sample, filtered beforehand. It holds 4,786 spots and the 10,486 genes that had at least 100 UMIs when the file was built (var["n_counts"]). The script that built it is not in this repository.

What the file contains
  • X: raw UMI counts
  • obs_names: the spot barcodes. Most carry a .1 or .2 suffix from the benchmark's copy (AAACAAGTATCTCCCA-1.2), so they differ from the original Space Ranger barcodes
  • obs["array_row"], obs["array_col"]: Visium grid coordinates
  • obsm["spatial"]: 2-D spot coordinates
  • obs["clusters"]: the annotated domain of each spot (Layer1 … Layer6, WM)
  • obs["pixel_row"], obs["pixel_col"]: pixel coordinates (read by SpaGCN)

Run a method lists which field each method reads.

When a step fails, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: How kDomainBench works
docs.text: kDomainBench gives ten methods one interface. Every method gets the same input .h5ad file and writes the same output, cluster_results.csv, with one domain label per spot. The estimated k is the number of distinct labels in that file.

docs.title: One call, three environments
docs.text:
The methods need incompatible software: R 4.4 with Bioconductor, PyTorch, and TensorFlow 2.15. So they run in three environments, and kdb.run starts each method in the right one:

  1. It looks up the method: its script in src/kdomainbench/methods/, its environment (your R, kdb_py or kdb_spatialde) and its arguments.
  2. It starts the script with that environment's Rscript or python, as a separate process whose working directory is the run folder.
  3. It saves everything the script prints to run.log, and measures the run time and the peak memory of the process.
  4. It reads cluster_results.csv back and writes run_info.json, with the device, run time, memory and estimated k, and packages.txt, the package versions of the environment.

Your own Python session needs only kdb_py. It never imports R, torch or TensorFlow for a run.

docs.title: CPU and GPU
docs.text:
Each method has one script for both devices, and the device is a command-line flag.

device="cpu" device="gpu" Visible GPUs none: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" gpu_id when given (CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID), else those already in CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, else GPU 0 CellCharter scVI trains with accelerator="cpu" accelerator="gpu" DeepST use_gpu=False use_gpu=True SpatialDE2 TensorFlow finds no GPU TensorFlow uses the visible GPU The other seven CPU CPU, with a UserWarning

The settings apply to the method's process only. run_info.json records both device_requested and device_used, the device the method was started with. They differ only for a CPU-only method asked to use the GPU (GPU or CPU?).

docs.title: Scores and metrics
docs.text: Scoring is separate from running. kdb.evaluate computes k error, ARI and NMI in Python. kdb.metrics computes the twelve metrics of the paper with the paper's own code, in R and in kdb_py (The twelve metrics of the paper).

docs.title: The ten methods
docs.text:
Method Model How k is selected PRECAST Spatial factor model + hidden Markov random field (HMRF) Fits k = 2 … kmax, picks one with a modified BIC (SelectModel) SC.MEB HMRF on 15 principal components Fits k = 2 … kmax, picks one by BIC (selectK) BayesSpace Bayesian spatial clustering with a Potts prior qTune gives a log-likelihood for k = 2 … kmax. The script takes its elbow, the k with the most negative second difference, which lies in 3 … kmax − 1 BNPSpace Bayesian nonparametric count model with feature selection Starts from kmax domains, adds and empties domains during MCMC, and reports those that hold spots. Its code allows at most 30 DR.SC Joint dimension reduction + spatial clustering Fits k = 2 … kmax, picks one with a modified BIC iSC.MEB Integrated HMRF on 15 principal components Fits k = 2 … kmax, picks one with a modified BIC (SelectModel) CellCharter scVI latent space, neighborhood aggregation, GMM ClusterAutoK: the k in 2 … kmax whose clustering is most stable over repeated fits (up to 10) DeepST Graph autoencoder on augmented expression Leiden resolution 0.1–2.5 with the highest Calinski–Harabasz score (priori=False). Ignores kmax SpaGCN Graph convolutional network + iterative clustering Louvain resolution 0.2–1.0 with the highest silhouette score. Ignores kmax SpatialDE2 Spatially variable genes + Bayesian tissue segmentation Variational segmentation with up to kmax classes. Empty classes are pruned

An HMRF and a Potts prior are spatial models in which neighboring spots tend to share a domain. BIC and its modified forms score how well each k fits and penalize the extra parameters. An elbow is the k after which the fit stops improving quickly.

Each method runs with the settings of its authors' tutorial. The calls are in the method scripts. Discover methods lists the environment and GPU support of each method, and Citation its publication.

docs.title: Method scripts
docs.text:
The scripts in src/kdomainbench/methods/ are copies of the scripts that ran the paper's benchmark, with only these changes:

  • run_cellcharter.py, run_deepst.py, run_spatialde.py: a --device cpu|gpu flag sets the device.
  • run_spagcn.py: hides the GPUs (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""), so SpaGCN always runs on the CPU.
  • bnpspace.R: finds its helper R and C++ sources through KDB_METHODS_DIR, set by kDomainBench, so it runs from any working directory.
  • bayesspace.R: copies array_row / array_col into row / col. BayesSpace 1.14 reads row / col, and versions from 1.16 read array_row / array_col. Both end up with the same coordinates.
  • scmeb.R: runs SC.MEB serially (parallel = FALSE). SCMEB_PARALLEL=TRUE runs it with SCMEB_CORES parallel workers (default 3).
  • drsc.R: no longer needs obs["clusters"], which DR.SC does not use, so it runs on a file without an annotation.
  • The Python scripts have a run_ prefix. Without it, cellcharter.py would import itself instead of the cellcharter package.

No script reads the reference annotation.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Five steps take you from finding a method to a figure of its domains. Only step 3 runs a method. It needs Linux and the environments from Installation. The outputs shown are those of the paper's benchmark (Citation) on sample 151509 (Example data). Key terms at the end of this page explains the words used on this site.

Run the code from the cloned repository folder, in Python or in Jupyter (FAQ), with the kdb_py environment active.

import kdomainbench as kdb

# 1. the methods, and which can use a GPU
kdb.list_methods()                  # ['PRECAST', 'SC.MEB', ..., 'SpaGCN', 'SpatialDE2']
kdb.list_methods(gpu_only=True)     # ['CellCharter', 'DeepST', 'SpatialDE2']

# 2. the example data: DLPFC sample 151509, reference k = 7
h5ad = "data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad"

# 3. run a method
clusters = kdb.run("SpaGCN", h5ad)
clusters["cluster"].nunique()       # 4, the estimated k

# 4. score it against the reference annotation
kdb.evaluate(clusters, h5ad)
# {'k_estimated': 4, 'k_reference': 7, 'k_error': -3,
#  'ARI': 0.4487, 'NMI': 0.5694, 'n_spots_scored': 4786}

# 5. plot its domains and save the figure
ax = kdb.pl.plot_spatial(clusters, h5ad, title="SpaGCN")
ax.figure.savefig("spagcn.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")

Each step has its own page:

  • Step 1: Discover methods, the method table and how each method picks k.
  • Step 3: Run a method, the arguments, the run folder, the input file and the GPU.
  • Step 4: Evaluate a run, what each score measures and how to compare many runs.
  • Step 5: Figures, every plot and its options.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
Steps 1, 3 and 4 from the shell:

terminal
kdomainbench methods                                     # the method table
kdomainbench run -m SpaGCN -i data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad     # writes kdb_results/SpaGCN/D3_151509_5k_cpu/
kdomainbench summarize --csv summary.csv --plot k.png    # scores every run, saves the table and the k figure

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Benchmark the ten methods: every method on sample 151509, with the table and the figures.
  • Your own data: from a Space Ranger folder to domains on the tissue.
  • API reference: every function and its parameters.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: .h5ad file The file format of AnnData, which scanpy uses: the counts of one sample, with obs (one row per spot), var (one row per gene) and obsm["spatial"] (the spot coordinates). spot One Visium capture spot: a row of the .h5ad file. spatial domain A group of spots with similar expression that also lie together, such as a cortical layer. k The number of spatial domains. The estimated k is the number of distinct labels a method returns. reference annotation The manual domain label of each spot, in obs["clusters"]. Its number of domains is the reference domain number, or reference k. k error Estimated k minus reference k. Negative means fewer domains than the annotation. ARI, NMI Two scores of how well a method's domains agree with the annotated ones. 1 is full agreement. kmax The largest k a method may consider, 30 by default. Most methods try k = 2 … kmax and pick one. DeepST and SpaGCN ignore it, and BNPSpace only starts from it (How each method picks k). device "cpu" or "gpu". Only CellCharter, DeepST and SpatialDE2 can use a GPU. conda environment A folder with its own Python and packages. kDomainBench uses two, kdb_py and kdb_spatialde (Installation). run folder The folder one run writes: cluster_results.csv, run.log, packages.txt and run_info.json (The run folder). summary table One row per run, from kdb.load_results, with the method, the estimated k and the scores.

docs.title: Run on a cluster
docs.text: This guide adapts Installation to a shared Linux cluster and runs each method as its own batch job. The examples use Slurm.

docs.title: 1. Install where there is internet
docs.text:
Create the environments in a project folder, which usually has more space than your home folder:

terminal
module load R                                    # if R comes as a module
KDB_ENVS_DIR=/project/envs bash envs/install_envs.sh
Rscript envs/install_r_packages.R                # the R packages, into your R
/project/envs/kdb_py/bin/kdomainbench check

kdomainbench check also downloads the reader the R methods need, so run it once on a node with internet (Troubleshooting).

docs.title: 2. Submit one job per method
docs.text:
Called by its full path, kdomainbench needs no conda activate and finds kdb_spatialde next to kdb_py. Each run writes its own folder, and the command exits with an error code when the method did not finish, so the scheduler marks the job as failed.

run_method.sh
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=10
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --time=02:00:00
module load R                # only for the six R methods
/project/envs/kdb_py/bin/kdomainbench run -m "$1" -i data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad -o results/
terminal
for m in PRECAST SC.MEB BayesSpace BNPSpace DR.SC iSC.MEB \
         CellCharter DeepST SpaGCN SpatialDE2; do
  sbatch run_method.sh "$m"
done

iSC.MEB starts 10 workers and PRECAST 4 (PRECAST_CORES). A job that reaches its time limit is stopped together with the method, and its run_info.json records "success": false.

docs.title: 3. Use a GPU
docs.text:
With -d gpu, the method uses the GPU your scheduler assigned through CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES. --gpu-id overrides it. Only CellCharter, DeepST and SpatialDE2 use the GPU.

run_gpu.sh
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --time=02:00:00
/project/envs/kdb_py/bin/kdomainbench run -m CellCharter DeepST SpatialDE2 -i data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad -d gpu -o results/

docs.title: 4. Collect the results
docs.text:
When the jobs are done:

terminal
/project/envs/kdb_py/bin/kdomainbench summarize results/ --csv summary.csv --plot k.png

docs.title: Your own data
docs.text:
This guide takes one 10x Visium sample from its Space Ranger folder to spatial domains on the tissue. It needs no annotation. If you have one, the last step also scores the methods. Key terms explains the words used here, such as kmax.

Summary

import kdomainbench as kdb
h5ad = "my_sample.h5ad"                         # built in step 1

results = kdb.run_all(h5ad, methods=["DR.SC", "SpaGCN", "iSC.MEB"], out_root="my_results/")
summary = kdb.load_results("my_results/")       # the k of each method
kdb.pl.plot_k_estimates(summary)
kdb.pl.plot_spatial_grid(results, h5ad)         # their domains on the tissue

docs.title: 1. Make the input file
docs.text:
Space Ranger writes one outs/ folder per sample. Start Python in the kdb_py environment (conda activate kdb_py), which has scanpy, and turn the folder into one .h5ad file:

import scanpy as sc

adata = sc.read_visium("path/to/sample/outs")     # reads filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 and spatial/
adata.var_names_make_unique()
adata = adata[adata.obs["in_tissue"] == 1].copy()

adata.obs["pixel_row"] = adata.obsm["spatial"][:, 1]
adata.obs["pixel_col"] = adata.obsm["spatial"][:, 0]
adata.obs["array_row"] = adata.obs["array_row"].astype(int)
adata.obs["array_col"] = adata.obs["array_col"].astype(int)

adata.write_h5ad("my_sample.h5ad")
print(adata)
# AnnData object with n_obs × n_vars = <spots> × <genes>
#     obs: 'in_tissue', 'array_row', 'array_col', 'pixel_row', 'pixel_col'
#     var: 'gene_ids', 'feature_types', 'genome'
#     uns: 'spatial'
#     obsm: 'spatial'

The file now holds the raw counts and the three sets of coordinates the methods read (Inputs). Keep the counts raw. The method scripts expect them and do their own normalization.

docs.title: 2. Run methods
docs.text:
Start with three methods to see that everything works:

import kdomainbench as kdb

h5ad = "my_sample.h5ad"
results = kdb.run_all(h5ad, methods=["DR.SC", "SpaGCN", "iSC.MEB"], out_root="my_results/")

Each method prints its output and, when it finishes, one line with its estimated k. A method that fails is reported as failed or not run and does not stop the others (Run several methods).

Each call runs the methods it names and leaves the other runs in my_results/ alone, so more methods can follow later, for example methods=["PRECAST", "SC.MEB"]. Without methods, all ten run.

docs.title: 3. Read the result
docs.text:
kdb.load_results collects every run of the folder, in this session or a later one:

summary = kdb.load_results("my_results/")
summary[["method", "k_estimated"]]
#     method  k_estimated
# 0    DR.SC           15
# 1   SpaGCN            4
# 2  iSC.MEB            3

ok = summary[summary["success"]]
results = {m: kdb.read_clusters(d) for m, d in zip(ok["method"], ok["out_dir"])}

The example output is that of the paper's benchmark runs on sample 151509. Without an annotation the k_error, ARI and NMI columns are empty, and the score_error column says no reference annotation.

Plot the estimates and the domains, and save the figures:

ax = kdb.pl.plot_k_estimates(summary)                      # one dot per method
ax.figure.savefig("k_estimates.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")

fig = kdb.pl.plot_spatial_grid(results, h5ad, ncols=3)     # one map per method
fig.savefig("domains.png", dpi=150)

kdb.pl.plot_spatial(results["SpaGCN"], h5ad, legend=True)  # one method, with its labels named

docs.title: The methods will disagree
docs.text:
Different methods return different numbers of domains for the same sample (Benchmark the ten methods). Read the estimates as candidates, not as the answer.

Check the domain sizes. A domain of a few spots adds to k without being a tissue region.

{name: sorted(c["cluster"].value_counts(), reverse=True) for name, c in results.items()}
# {'DR.SC': [773, 718, 647, 468, 460, 270, 269, 236, 224, 157, 149, 137, 122, 106, 50],
#  'SpaGCN': [1556, 1513, 1288, 429],
#  'iSC.MEB': [3342, 1275, 169]}

Check how far the methods agree. The ARI between the domains of two methods is 1 when they are the same and near 0 when they are no more alike than by chance:

import pandas as pd

agreement = pd.DataFrame({a: {b: kdb.evaluate(results[a], results[b])["ARI"] for b in results}
                          for a in results})
agreement.round(2)

A cross table shows where two methods differ. Each row is a SpaGCN domain and each column a DR.SC domain, so a row spread over two columns is a domain that DR.SC splits:

pd.crosstab(results["SpaGCN"]["cluster"].rename("SpaGCN"), results["DR.SC"]["cluster"].rename("DR.SC"))

Compare each map with what you know of the tissue: the histology image, marker genes, the expected anatomy. This draws the domains on the image:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scanpy as sc

adata = sc.read_h5ad(h5ad)
for name, labels in results.items():
    adata.obs[name] = labels["cluster"].reindex(adata.obs_names).astype("category")
sc.pl.spatial(adata, color=["SpaGCN", "DR.SC"], show=False)    # add a gene name to see a marker gene
plt.savefig("domains_on_image.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")

Keep kmax the same across the methods that use it, and report the k of every method you ran, not one number chosen afterwards. This site does not rank the methods. The paper compares them across many datasets (Citation).

docs.title: 4. If you have an annotation
docs.text:
A manual annotation, for example exported from Loupe Browser as a CSV file with one row per barcode, becomes the reference annotation in obs["clusters"]:

import anndata as ad
import pandas as pd

adata = ad.read_h5ad("my_sample.h5ad")
labels = pd.read_csv("annotation.csv", index_col=0).iloc[:, 0]     # barcode, label
labels.index.isin(adata.obs_names).mean()                           # 1.0: every barcode is a spot of the file
adata.obs["clusters"] = labels.reindex(adata.obs_names)             # spots without a label stay empty
adata.write_h5ad("my_sample.h5ad")

The runs need not be repeated. load_results reads the annotation from the file and now scores each run:

summary = kdb.load_results("my_results/")
summary[["method", "k_estimated", "k_reference", "k_error", "ARI", "NMI"]]
kdb.k_accuracy(summary)

Evaluate a run explains the scores.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Most sections start with the message you see in Python. From the command line the same text follows kdomainbench: error:, [kdomainbench] or not scored. A failed run keeps its whole output in run.log in its run folder, and a failed metric call in metric.log.

docs.title: A method stopped
docs.text:
MethodFailed: <method> failed (exit <code>), see <run folder>/run.log

The method itself stopped. The message ends with the last 20 lines of its log, which usually name the cause. For a missing package, run kdomainbench check.

docs.title: An environment is not found
docs.text:
FileNotFoundError: conda env 'kdb_py' not found: create it with 'bash envs/install_envs.sh' ...
FileNotFoundError: Rscript not found: install R 4.4 or later, or load it ...

Create the environment (Installation), or point kDomainBench to it with the matching variable (Environment variables).

docs.title: A variable points to the wrong file
docs.text:
FileNotFoundError: KDB_PY_PYTHON points to <path>, which is not an interpreter

The variable holds a path that does not exist or cannot be executed. It must be the environment's python (or Rscript for KDB_RSCRIPT), not its folder.

docs.title: The labels and the annotation share no spot
docs.text:
ValueError: the clusters and the reference annotation share no spot. Both must be indexed by the same spot barcodes

The labels and the annotation use different spot barcodes, for example with and without the -1 suffix. Both must be indexed by the obs_names of the input file.

docs.title: The file has no annotation
docs.text:
KeyError: no reference annotation: obs has no column 'clusters' (its columns: ...)

The input file has no obs["clusters"]. Add the annotation (Your own data), or name the column that holds it with reference_key= (--reference-key on the command line).

docs.title: BNPSpace and kmax
docs.text:
ValueError: BNPSpace accepts kmax up to 30

BNPSpace's own code allows at most 30 domains. Run it with kmax=30 (-k 30) or less.

docs.title: The stack limit
docs.text:
[kdomainbench] could not raise the stack limit ...

PRECAST and iSC.MEB need more stack memory than most systems allow by default, and kDomainBench raises the limit for them (ulimit -s unlimited). This line in their log means your system forbids it. The method may then stop with a stack error. Ask your administrator to raise the hard stack limit (ulimit -Hs shows it).

docs.title: The first R run is slow, or fails without internet
docs.text: zellkonverter reads .h5ad files through a Python environment that basilisk downloads on first use into ~/.cache/R/basilisk, several hundred MB. kdomainbench check triggers the download, so run it once where there is internet. BASILISK_EXTERNAL_DIR moves the folder.

docs.title: Installing louvain fails
docs.text: SpaGCN needs louvain, which has no prebuilt package (wheel) for Python 3.12, so pip builds it from source. That needs a C++ compiler and cmake on PATH.

docs.title: PRECAST uses too many cores
docs.text: It forks workers. PRECAST_CORES caps them (default 4).

docs.title: The twelve metrics fail
docs.text:
MetricsFailed: metrics.R failed (exit 1), see <run folder>/metric.log
MetricsFailed: no value for SCS (PASTE's code returns no SCS with pandas 3 or later in kdb_py), see <run folder>/metric.log

The first is most often a missing R package: install them as in The metric packages and run kdomainbench check --metrics. The second means the Python that runs scs.py has pandas 3 or later. It must be kdb_py, or a Python named in KDB_PY_PYTHON with pandas below 3.

More questions: FAQ.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
The kdomainbench command does from the shell what the Python API does. It is installed with the package, in kdb_py.

Command Does Python kdomainbench methods Print the methods: language, environment, GPU, use of kmax. kdb.list_methods kdomainbench check Start each environment once and print its key packages. kdomainbench run Run methods on an .h5ad file. kdb.run_all kdomainbench metrics Compute the twelve metrics of every finished run. kdb.metrics kdomainbench summarize Score every run and print the tables. kdb.load_results, kdb.k_accuracy

kdomainbench --version prints the package version, and kdomainbench <command> --help the options below. Environment variables tell the command where the environments are.

Exit status Meaning 0 Done. summarize also returns 0 when runs failed or could not be scored, as long as one run succeeded: its not scored lines say why. 1 An environment is missing or fails (check, run), a method did not finish (run), a metric could not be computed (metrics), no run succeeded (metrics, summarize), a file or folder was not found, or a value cannot be used (an unknown method, a kmax a method does not accept, an --h5ad file that matches no run). 2 The command line cannot be parsed: an unknown command or option, a missing argument, a value of the wrong kind (-k abc, -d tpu). The usage line is printed. 128 + signal run was stopped by a signal, for example by scancel or a time limit.

A fatal error is one line that starts with kdomainbench: error:. run names the methods that did not finish in a kdomainbench: warning: line, and check marks an environment as MISSING or FAILED.

docs.title: kdomainbench methods
docs.text:
kdomainbench methods

Prints one line per method (Discover methods).

docs.title: kdomainbench check
docs.text:
kdomainbench check [--gpu] [--gpu-id N] [--metrics]

Starts each environment once, prints its key packages, looks for every R package the method scripts load and reads a small .h5ad file from R (Installation).

Option Meaning --gpu Check with the GPU visible, and fail when none is. --gpu-id N GPU to make visible with --gpu. Default: those in CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, else 0. --metrics Also compute the twelve metrics on a small test sample.

docs.title: kdomainbench run
docs.text:
kdomainbench run -m METHOD [METHOD ...] -i FILE [-k KMAX] [-d {cpu,gpu}] [--gpu-id N] [-o DIR]

Runs the methods one after another, as kdb.run_all does.

Option Meaning -m, --method Method names as kdomainbench methods prints them (case-insensitive), or all for all ten. -i, --input Input .h5ad file. -k, --kmax Largest number of domains a method may consider, at least 2. Default: 30. BNPSpace accepts at most 30, and DeepST and SpaGCN do not use it. -d, --device cpu or gpu. A method without GPU code runs on the CPU and warns. Default: cpu. --gpu-id N GPU for -d gpu. Default: those in CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, else 0. -o, --out Results folder. Each run goes to DIR/<method>/<dataset>_<device> and replaces a run already there. Default: kdb_results. terminal
kdomainbench run -m SpaGCN DR.SC -i data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad -k 30

docs.title: kdomainbench metrics
docs.text:
kdomainbench metrics [--h5ad FILE] [--force] [root]

Prints the twelve metrics of the paper for every finished run under root, one row per run (Evaluate a run). A run without metric.csv is computed first, which needs the metric packages (Installation) and the annotation in obs["clusters"].

Option Meaning root Results folder. Default: kdb_results. --h5ad FILE An input file named <dataset>.h5ad, for runs whose recorded input file is not on this machine: D3_151509_5k.h5ad for the runs of D3_151509_5k. Repeat it for several datasets. --force Compute again for runs that already have metric.csv.

docs.title: kdomainbench summarize
docs.text:
kdomainbench summarize [--h5ad FILE] [--reference-key COLUMN] [--csv FILE] [--plot FILE] [root]

Prints the main columns of the summary table of every run under root, why runs could not be scored, and the k_accuracy table (Evaluate a run).

Option Meaning root Results folder. Default: kdb_results. --h5ad FILE An input file named <dataset>.h5ad, as for metrics. --reference-key COLUMN obs column with the reference annotation. Default: clusters. --csv FILE Also save the table of runs, with every column, as a CSV file. --plot FILE Also save the k-estimate figure. The extension gives the format (PNG, PDF, SVG). terminal
kdomainbench summarize --csv summary.csv --plot k.png

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: List the methods and see what each one needs. These calls run nothing.

docs.title: list_methods
docs.text:
list_methods(gpu_only=False)

Return the names of the methods.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION gpu_only

True = only the methods that can run on a GPU.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

RETURNS DESCRIPTION list of str

Method names, R methods first.

Examples:

>>> kdb.list_methods()
['PRECAST', 'SC.MEB', 'BayesSpace', 'BNPSpace', 'DR.SC', 'iSC.MEB',
 'CellCharter', 'DeepST', 'SpaGCN', 'SpatialDE2']
>>> kdb.list_methods(gpu_only=True)
['CellCharter', 'DeepST', 'SpatialDE2']

docs.title: get_method
docs.text:
get_method(name)

Return one method's settings.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION name

Method name, case-insensitive. Aliases such as "drsc", "iscmeb" or "spatialde" work too.

TYPE: str

RETURNS DESCRIPTION Method

Its language, environment, GPU support, use of kmax and reference.

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

Unknown method name.

Examples:

>>> m = kdb.get_method("cellcharter")
>>> m.name, m.language, m.env, m.gpu, m.uses_kmax
('CellCharter', 'Python', 'py', True, True)

docs.title: Method dataclass
docs.text:
One method: its script, its environment and how it is called.

Get one with get_method. You do not create them yourself.

ATTRIBUTE DESCRIPTION name

Canonical name, e.g. "CellCharter".

TYPE: str

language

"R" or "Python".

TYPE: str

env

Environment key: "r" (your R), "py" (kdb_py) or "spatialde" (kdb_spatialde).

TYPE: str

script

The method's script in kdomainbench/methods/.

TYPE: str

argv

(h5ad, run_folder, kmax) -> list[str], the script's arguments.

TYPE: callable

gpu

True if device="gpu" really runs the method on a GPU.

TYPE: bool

uses_kmax

False if the method chooses k by itself and ignores kmax.

TYPE: bool

big_stack

True if the method needs ulimit -s unlimited.

TYPE: bool

kmax_limit

Largest kmax the method accepts, if it has a limit.

TYPE: int or None

reference

The method's documentation or repository.

TYPE: str

aliases

Other accepted names, e.g. ("drsc",).

TYPE: tuple of str

Examples:

>>> m = kdb.get_method("BNPSpace")
>>> m.language, m.env, m.gpu, m.kmax_limit
('R', 'r', False, 30)

docs.title: All methods
docs.text:
kdb.METHODS is a dict from each method's name to its Method record, in the order of kdb.list_methods().

[m.name for m in kdb.METHODS.values() if m.language == "R"]
# ['PRECAST', 'SC.MEB', 'BayesSpace', 'BNPSpace', 'DR.SC', 'iSC.MEB']

docs.title: Figures
docs.text: kdb.pl draws the benchmark's figures with matplotlib. Each function returns its axes or figure. These calls need only the kdomainbench package, not the method environments.

docs.title: plot_k_estimates
docs.text:
plot_k_estimates(summary, ax=None, k_reference=None)

Plot the estimated k of each method against the reference domain number.

One row per method and one dot per estimate, laid out as Fig. 2b and 2c of the paper. A dashed line marks the reference domain number. A dot is blue when the method returned fewer domains than the reference, green when it returned as many, and red when it returned more. Methods are sorted by the median of their dots.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION summary

The table from load_results.

TYPE: DataFrame

ax

Axes to draw on. Default: a new figure.

TYPE: Axes DEFAULT: None

k_reference

Reference domain number of every run, for a file without an annotation. Default: the k_reference column of summary.

TYPE: int DEFAULT: None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION Axes

The plot. ax.figure.savefig(..., bbox_inches="tight") saves it with its legend.

RAISES DESCRIPTION TypeError

summary is not a table.

KeyError

summary lacks a column of the load_results table.

ValueError

summary has no successful run.

Notes
  • Runs of a method at the same place on the x axis share one dot, and its area gives their number.
  • When the runs have different reference domain numbers (several datasets), the x axis is the k error, estimated k − reference k.
  • Runs without a reference annotation are left out when other runs have one. When no run has one, the dots are gray and there is no line.
  • The paper's panels also shade a dot by the size of its error. Here the position on the x axis gives the size, and the color only the direction.

Examples:

>>> summary = kdb.load_results("kdb_results")
>>> ax = kdb.pl.plot_k_estimates(summary)
>>> ax.figure.savefig("k_estimates.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")

docs.title: plot_metrics
docs.text:
plot_metrics(summary, ax=None)

Plot the metrics of each method as a matrix of bars.

One row per method and one column per metric, laid out as Fig. 2f of the paper. The length of a bar is the value of the metric, on the metric's own axis below the column. The fill is the rank of the method among the methods for that metric: the darker, the better. The arrow above a column says whether higher or lower is better.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION summary

The table from load_results. The columns of the twelve metrics are there for the runs scored with metrics. A method whose runs were not scored has n/a in the other columns, and a table without any scored run shows ARI and NMI only.

TYPE: DataFrame

ax

Axes to draw on. Default: a new figure.

TYPE: Axes DEFAULT: None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION Axes

The plot. ax.figure.savefig(..., bbox_inches="tight") saves it.

RAISES DESCRIPTION TypeError

summary is not a table.

KeyError

summary lacks a column of the load_results table.

ValueError

summary has no successful run, or none of its runs has a metric value.

Notes
  • With several runs per method, a bar is the mean over the runs that have a value, and the whisker is their standard deviation. Filter summary first to compare within one dataset or device. In the paper the datasets of each data source are averaged first, and a bar is the mean over the five sources.
  • An axis runs from 0 to a round number above the highest value, and from below 0 when a value is negative. The axes of the paper's panel are set by hand and do not all start at 0.
  • Methods are listed in the order of their first successful run in summary.
  • Methods with the same value share the better rank. n/a marks a metric without a value, such as SCS of a run with one domain.

Examples:

>>> summary = kdb.load_results("kdb_results")
>>> ax = kdb.pl.plot_metrics(summary)
>>> ax.figure.savefig("metrics.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")

docs.title: run
docs.text:
run(method, h5ad, kmax=30, device='cpu', out_root='kdb_results', gpu_id=None, verbose=True)

Run one method on one .h5ad file and return its spatial domains.

The method runs in the environment it needs, as a separate process, and writes to its run folder <out_root>/<method>/<dataset>_<device>. A run into a folder that already holds a run replaces it.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION method

Method name, case-insensitive, from list_methods.

TYPE: str

h5ad

Input .h5ad file with raw counts in X. The R methods read obs["array_row"] and obs["array_col"], SpaGCN obs["pixel_row"] and obs["pixel_col"], and CellCharter, DeepST and SpatialDE2 obsm["spatial"]. An AnnData object in memory is not accepted: save it with adata.write_h5ad(...) first.

TYPE: str or path

kmax

Largest number of domains the method may consider, at least 2. DeepST and SpaGCN ignore it. BNPSpace starts from it and accepts at most 30.

TYPE: int DEFAULT: 30

device

"cpu" or "gpu". With "gpu", CellCharter, DeepST and SpatialDE2 are started with a GPU visible. The other methods have no GPU code and run on the CPU, with a warning.

TYPE: str DEFAULT: 'cpu'

out_root

Folder that collects the run folders, the same as for run_all.

TYPE: str or path DEFAULT: 'kdb_results'

gpu_id

GPU to use with device="gpu", as numbered by nvidia-smi. Default: the GPUs already named in CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, as a job scheduler sets it, else GPU 0.

TYPE: int or str DEFAULT: None

verbose

Print the method's output while it runs.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

One row per spot, indexed by spot_id, with the domain label (as a string) in cluster.

RAISES DESCRIPTION MethodFailed

The method stopped with an error or wrote no labels. run_info.json records the run with "success": false.

FileNotFoundError

h5ad does not exist or is a folder, or the method's environment is missing. Nothing is written.

ValueError

Unknown method or device, an input file that is not .h5ad, or a kmax the method does not accept.

WARNS DESCRIPTION UserWarning

device="gpu" for a method without GPU code.

Notes

The run folder holds:

  • cluster_results.csv: the label of each spot.
  • run.log: everything the method printed.
  • packages.txt: the packages and versions of the method's environment.

  • run_info.json, with these fields:

    • method, dataset (the file name without .h5ad), h5ad (the input path), kmax.
    • device_requested, and device_used, which is "cpu" for a method without GPU code. gpu_id: the GPU of a GPU run.
    • started, wall_time_s (the whole run, data loading included) and peak_rss_mb (peak memory of the method's largest process, 1 GB = 1024 MB, without its worker processes and the GPU).
    • returncode and success. A successful run adds n_spots (spots with a label) and k_estimated.
    • kdomainbench (the package version), command (the call of the method script, started in the run folder, to rerun it by hand) and env (the environment variables that change what the method does).

Examples:

>>> clusters = kdb.run("SpaGCN", "data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad", kmax=30)
>>> clusters["cluster"].nunique()
4
>>> kdb.run("CellCharter", "data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad", device="gpu", gpu_id=0)

docs.title: run_all
docs.text:
run_all(h5ad, kmax=30, device='cpu', methods=None, out_root='kdb_results', gpu_id=None, verbose=True)

Run several methods on one .h5ad file, one after another.

A method that fails, or whose environment is missing, is reported and skipped, so it does not stop the others. At the end one warning names every method that did not finish.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION h5ad

Input file, see run.

TYPE: str or path

kmax

Largest number of domains the methods may consider. BNPSpace accepts at most 30: for a larger kmax, leave it out with methods=.

TYPE: int DEFAULT: 30

device

"cpu" or "gpu", see run.

TYPE: str DEFAULT: 'cpu'

methods

Methods to run. Default: all ten. Each one runs again, also when out_root already holds a run of it.

TYPE: str or list of str DEFAULT: None

out_root

Each method writes to <out_root>/<method>/<dataset>_<device>.

TYPE: str or path DEFAULT: 'kdb_results'

gpu_id

GPU for device="gpu", see run.

TYPE: int or str DEFAULT: None

verbose

Print the methods' output while they run.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

RETURNS DESCRIPTION dict

Method name -> its clusters, for the methods that succeeded.

RAISES DESCRIPTION FileNotFoundError

h5ad does not exist or is a folder.

ValueError

An unknown method or device, an input file that is not .h5ad, or a kmax that one of the methods does not accept. Raised before the first method starts.

WARNS DESCRIPTION UserWarning

Some methods did not finish. The warning names them and their logs.

Examples:

>>> results = kdb.run_all("data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad", kmax=30)
>>> results = kdb.run_all("data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad", methods=["DR.SC", "SC.MEB"])
>>> sorted(results)
['DR.SC', 'SC.MEB']

docs.title: evaluate
docs.text:
evaluate(clusters, reference)

Score one run against the reference annotation.

k_estimated counts every label the method returned and k_reference every annotated domain. ARI and NMI use the spots that have both a label and an annotation. NMI is normalized by the arithmetic mean of the two entropies (the scikit-learn default).

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION clusters

The run's labels, as returned by run or read_clusters, or its run folder.

TYPE: DataFrame or Series or path

reference

The .h5ad file or AnnData object (its obs["clusters"] is read), the labels from reference_annotation, or another run (its labels or its run folder) to see how far two methods agree. For another obs column, pass kdb.reference_annotation(h5ad, reference_key=...).

TYPE: path or AnnData or Series or DataFrame

RETURNS DESCRIPTION dict

k_estimated, k_reference, k_error (estimated − reference), ARI and NMI (rounded to 4 digits, while metrics gives full precision) and n_spots_scored (the spots ARI and NMI were computed on).

RAISES DESCRIPTION FileNotFoundError

The run folder or the .h5ad file is missing.

KeyError

The file has no obs["clusters"].

TypeError

clusters or reference is not one of the types above.

ValueError

No spot has both a label and an annotation (the two do not use the same barcodes), a barcode occurs twice, or the file is not an .h5ad file.

Examples:

>>> kdb.evaluate("kdb_results/SpaGCN/D3_151509_5k_cpu", "data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad")
{'k_estimated': 4, 'k_reference': 7, 'k_error': -3, 'ARI': 0.4487, 'NMI': 0.5694, 'n_spots_scored': 4786}

docs.title: metrics
docs.text:
metrics(run, h5ad=None, recompute=False)

Compute the twelve metrics of the paper for one finished run.

Eleven metrics come from metrics.R, run in your R, and SCS from scs.py, run in kdb_py. The result is saved as metric.csv in the run folder, where load_results picks it up, and a later call reads it back.

The input file needs pixel coordinates in obs["pixel_row"], obs["pixel_col"] and obsm["spatial"], and a reference annotation in obs["clusters"] with at least two domains. Every spot needs both an annotation and a label from the run.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION run

A run folder with cluster_results.csv.

TYPE: str or path

h5ad

The input file. Default: the path recorded in the run's run_info.json. It is read only when the metrics are computed, not when metric.csv is read back.

TYPE: str or path DEFAULT: None

recompute

True = compute again when the run folder already has metric.csv, for example after the annotation changed.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

RETURNS DESCRIPTION Series

ARI, spARI, NMI, FM, AMI, Purity, HOM, COM, PAS, CHAOS, LISI and SCS. SCS is NaN for a run with one domain.

RAISES DESCRIPTION MetricsFailed

The metric code stopped, for example because a package is missing or a spot has no label.

FileNotFoundError

run is not a run folder, or the input file or an environment is missing.

Examples:

>>> kdb.metrics("kdb_results/DR.SC/D3_151509_5k_cpu").round(4).head(3)
metric
ARI      0.2333
spARI    0.2110
NMI      0.4826
Name: value, dtype: float64

The message names the run's metric.log, which holds the output of the metric code.

docs.title: load_results
docs.text:
load_results(root='kdb_results', reference_key='clusters', score=True, h5ad=None)

Collect every run under a folder into one table.

Reads each run_info.json under root, at any depth. Each successful run is scored against the reference annotation of its own .h5ad file.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION root

Folder that holds the run folders.

TYPE: str or path DEFAULT: 'kdb_results'

reference_key

Column of obs with the reference annotation.

TYPE: str DEFAULT: 'clusters'

score

False = only collect the run records, without scoring.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

h5ad

Where the input file is now, when the runs were made elsewhere: one file when all runs are of one dataset, else {dataset: file}. Default: the path recorded in each run_info.json.

TYPE: str or path or dict DEFAULT: None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

One row per run, always with method, dataset, device_requested, device_used, kmax, k_estimated, k_reference, k_error, ARI, NMI, wall_time_s, peak_rss_mb, success, n_spots_scored, score_error and out_dir (the run folder), then the other fields of run_info.json except command (n_spots is the number of labeled spots). A run that could not be scored, for example because its file has no annotation, has the reason in score_error and no k_reference, k_error, ARI or NMI. With reference_key="clusters", a run with a metric.csv from metrics also has the ten other metrics of the paper as columns. The table is empty, with the columns above, when root holds no run.

RAISES DESCRIPTION FileNotFoundError

root is not a folder, or a file given as h5ad does not exist.

ValueError

h5ad is one file and the runs are of several datasets, or h5ad names a dataset that has no run under root.

Examples:

>>> summary = kdb.load_results("kdb_results")
>>> summary[["method", "k_estimated", "k_error", "ARI"]].head(3)
        method  k_estimated  k_error     ARI
0     BNPSpace            2       -5  0.0480
1   BayesSpace            4       -3  0.3745
2  CellCharter            2       -5  0.3657

docs.text:
k_accuracy(summary)

Summarize how well each method estimates k.

Each method is summarized over all its runs in summary. Filter the table first to compare within one dataset or device. Failed runs and runs without a reference annotation are left out.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION summary

The table from load_results.

TYPE: DataFrame

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

One row per method, best first (smallest mean absolute k error, then highest mean ARI): runs, mean_abs_k_error, exact_rate (fraction of runs with exactly the reference k) and mean_ARI. Empty when no run has a reference annotation.

method

docs.text:
set_env(key, interpreter=None, r_lib=None)

Point one method environment at an interpreter, for this Python session.

An environment variable (KDB_PY_PYTHON, KDB_SPATIALDE_PYTHON, KDB_RSCRIPT, KDB_METRICS_RSCRIPT, KDB_R_LIB) still wins over this setting.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION key

"py" (kdb_py), "spatialde" (kdb_spatialde), "r" (your R) or "metrics" (the R of the metric code, when it is not the R of the methods).

TYPE: str

interpreter

The environment's python, or Rscript for "r" and "metrics". It is checked when a method starts, not here.

TYPE: str or path DEFAULT: None

r_lib

An isolated R library for the R methods, whatever key is. They then see only this library and base R. The metric code uses it too, unless "metrics" names its own Rscript.

Unknown key.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Meaning Default KDB_PY_PYTHON python of kdb_py the conda env kdb_py KDB_SPATIALDE_PYTHON python of kdb_spatialde the conda env kdb_spatialde KDB_RSCRIPT Rscript for the R methods Rscript on PATH KDB_R_LIB separate R library. The R methods see only it and base R none KDB_METRICS_RSCRIPT Rscript for the metric code, when it is not the R of the methods. KDB_R_LIB is not applied to it the R of the methods PRECAST_CORES worker processes of PRECAST 4 SCMEB_PARALLEL TRUE = run SC.MEB with parallel workers FALSE SCMEB_CORES worker processes of SC.MEB when SCMEB_PARALLEL=TRUE 3

Without the variables, the conda envs are looked for next to the environment kdomainbench runs in, then under $CONDA_EXE, $MAMBA_EXE, $CONDA_PREFIX and ~/anaconda3, ~/miniconda3, ~/mambaforge, ~/miniforge3, ~/.conda. Environments created together by envs/install_envs.sh are therefore found without any setting, also in a folder given with KDB_ENVS_DIR.

docs.title: Benchmark the ten methods
docs.text:
This tutorial runs all ten methods on sample 151509 and asks how close each one gets to the reference domain number (reference k). The table and figures below show the runs of the paper's benchmark on this sample, one per method.

Summary

import kdomainbench as kdb
h5ad = "data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad"

results = kdb.run_all(h5ad, kmax=30, device="cpu", out_root="bench/")
summary = kdb.load_results("bench/")
kdb.k_accuracy(summary)
kdb.pl.plot_k_estimates(summary)
kdb.pl.plot_spatial_grid(results, h5ad)

docs.title: 1. The data
docs.text:
D3_151509_5k.h5ad is sample 151509 (Example data). Its reference annotation has 7 domains, six cortical layers and white matter: k = 7.

import kdomainbench as kdb

h5ad = "data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad"
reference = kdb.reference_annotation(h5ad).to_frame("cluster")
kdb.pl.plot_spatial(reference, h5ad, title="Reference annotation (k = 7)", legend=True)

docs.title: 2. Run every method
docs.text:
results = kdb.run_all(h5ad, kmax=30, device="cpu", out_root="bench/")

run_all runs all ten with kmax = 30 and otherwise as their method scripts set them.

docs.title: 3. Estimated k and accuracy
docs.text:
summary = kdb.load_results("bench/")
best_first = kdb.k_accuracy(summary).index      # smallest k error first, then highest ARI
summary.set_index("method").loc[best_first, ["k_estimated", "k_error", "ARI", "NMI"]]
Method Estimated k k error ARI NMI PRECAST 5 -2 0.26 0.38 DeepST 4 -3 0.54 0.64 SpaGCN 4 -3 0.45 0.57 BayesSpace 4 -3 0.37 0.58 SpatialDE2 10 +3 0.36 0.53 SC.MEB 10 +3 0.34 0.54 iSC.MEB 3 -4 0.38 0.52 CellCharter 2 -5 0.37 0.46 BNPSpace 2 -5 0.05 0.16 DR.SC 15 +8 0.23 0.48

The methods are sorted by the size of their k error (estimated k − reference k), then by ARI. ARI and NMI compare the domains with the annotated ones (Evaluate a run). The raw numbers are in summary_5k.csv.

kdb.pl.plot_k_estimates(summary)

Blue dots are below the reference k and red ones above. A dot on it would be green.

docs.title: 4. The domains on the tissue
docs.text:
fig = kdb.pl.plot_spatial_grid(results, h5ad, ncols=5)

Compare each map with the reference annotation above. Colors follow the sorted label names, so the same color in two maps does not mean the same domain.

docs.title: 5. The twelve metrics
docs.text:
kdb.metrics scores a run with the twelve metrics of the paper, and kdb.pl.plot_metrics draws them:

for run in summary.loc[summary["success"], "out_dir"]:
    kdb.metrics(run)                      # saved as metric.csv in the run folder
summary = kdb.load_results("bench/")      # read again, now with the metrics
kdb.pl.plot_metrics(summary)

A darker bar is a better rank among the ten methods (Evaluate a run explains the figure).

docs.title: From the shell
docs.text:
terminal
kdomainbench run -m all -i data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad -o bench/
kdomainbench metrics bench/
kdomainbench summarize bench/ --csv summary.csv --plot k.png

The first command runs the methods one after another, and the second needs the metric packages (Installation).

docs.title: Discover methods
docs.text:
kDomainBench runs ten methods that estimate the number of spatial domains. This page shows how to list them, what each one needs, and how each one picks k.

Summary

import kdomainbench as kdb
kdb.list_methods()                    # all ten
kdb.list_methods(gpu_only=True)       # the three that can use a GPU
m = kdb.get_method("DR.SC")           # one method's settings

docs.title: List the methods
docs.text:
import kdomainbench as kdb
kdb.list_methods()
# ['PRECAST', 'SC.MEB', 'BayesSpace', 'BNPSpace', 'DR.SC', 'iSC.MEB',
#  'CellCharter', 'DeepST', 'SpaGCN', 'SpatialDE2']

kdomainbench methods prints them as a table:

kdomainbench methods
method      language env        GPU  uses kmax
PRECAST     R        r          -    yes
SC.MEB      R        r          -    yes
BayesSpace  R        r          -    yes
BNPSpace    R        r          -    yes
DR.SC       R        r          -    yes
iSC.MEB     R        r          -    yes
CellCharter Python   py         yes  yes
DeepST      Python   py         yes  no (auto)
SpaGCN      Python   py         -    no (auto)
SpatialDE2  Python   spatialde  yes  yes

env is the environment the method runs in: r is your R, py is kdb_py and spatialde is kdb_spatialde (Installation).

docs.title: Filter by what you need
docs.text:
Three methods can use a GPU:

kdb.list_methods(gpu_only=True)
# ['CellCharter', 'DeepST', 'SpatialDE2']

Two methods do not take kmax:

[m for m in kdb.list_methods() if not kdb.get_method(m).uses_kmax]
# ['DeepST', 'SpaGCN']

docs.title: Inspect a single method
docs.text:
m = kdb.get_method("cellcharter")      # case-insensitive, and aliases such as "drsc" work too
m.name, m.language, m.env, m.gpu, m.uses_kmax
# ('CellCharter', 'Python', 'py', True, True)
m.reference
# 'https://cellcharter.readthedocs.io/'
m.script
# 'run_cellcharter.py'

kdb.Method lists every field of the record.

docs.title: How each method picks k
docs.text:
The ten methods choose k in three ways:

  • Fit every k and keep the best. PRECAST, SC.MEB, BayesSpace, DR.SC, iSC.MEB and CellCharter fit k = 2 … kmax and keep one by a model-selection score (BIC, clustering stability or a likelihood elbow).
  • Start high and drop empty domains. BNPSpace and SpatialDE2 start from kmax domains and report those that hold spots at the end. BNPSpace can also add domains, up to 30.
  • Tune a resolution. DeepST and SpaGCN try a range of clustering resolutions and keep the best-scoring one. The number of domains follows from it.

How kDomainBench works has each method's model and criterion.

Next: Run a method.

docs.title: Evaluate a run
docs.text:
A run gives one domain label per spot. kdb.evaluate compares them with the reference annotation: how far the estimated k is from the reference k, and how well the domains agree with the annotated ones. The examples score the runs of Run a method, and the input file needs a reference annotation in obs["clusters"]. The outputs shown are those of the paper's benchmark runs on sample 151509.

Summary

import kdomainbench as kdb
h5ad = "data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad"

clusters = kdb.read_clusters("kdb_results/SpaGCN/D3_151509_5k_cpu")  # or what kdb.run returns
kdb.evaluate(clusters, h5ad)                  # one run: k error, ARI, NMI
summary = kdb.load_results("kdb_results")     # every run under kdb_results/, scored
kdb.k_accuracy(summary)                       # one row per method
kdb.metrics("kdb_results/DR.SC/D3_151509_5k_cpu")    # the twelve metrics of the paper
kdb.pl.plot_metrics(kdb.load_results("kdb_results")) # the metrics as a figure

docs.title: Score one run
docs.text:
clusters = kdb.read_clusters("kdb_results/SpaGCN/D3_151509_5k_cpu")
kdb.evaluate(clusters, h5ad)
# {'k_estimated': 4, 'k_reference': 7, 'k_error': -3,
#  'ARI': 0.4487, 'NMI': 0.5694, 'n_spots_scored': 4786}

The second argument is the .h5ad file, whose obs["clusters"] holds the reference annotation, or the annotation itself as a Series indexed by spot:

reference = kdb.reference_annotation(h5ad)                       # obs["clusters"], spots without a label dropped
reference = kdb.reference_annotation(h5ad, reference_key="layer_guess")    # another column
kdb.evaluate(clusters, reference)

Another run in its place compares two methods (Your own data).

docs.title: What each score measures
docs.text:
Score Meaning Best k_estimated number of distinct labels the method returned k_reference number of distinct labels in the reference annotation k_error k_estimated − k_reference. Negative means fewer domains than the annotation 0 ARI adjusted Rand index between the labels and the annotation 1 NMI normalized mutual information between the labels and the annotation, with the arithmetic mean of the two entropies as the norm 1 n_spots_scored spots that have both a label and an annotation. ARI and NMI use these

Labels and annotation are matched by spot barcode. kdb.evaluate raises a ValueError when they share no spot or when a barcode occurs twice. A partial match is scored without a warning, so check n_spots_scored.

docs.title: Score many runs
docs.text:
kdb.load_results reads every run_info.json under a folder and scores each successful run against its own .h5ad file. The result has one row per run:

summary = kdb.load_results("kdb_results")
summary[["method", "k_estimated", "k_reference", "k_error", "ARI", "NMI"]]
#         method  k_estimated  k_reference  k_error     ARI     NMI
# 0     BNPSpace            2            7       -5  0.0480  0.1604
# 1   BayesSpace            4            7       -3  0.3745  0.5776
# 2  CellCharter            2            7       -5  0.3657  0.4609
# ...

kdb.k_accuracy gives one row per method, the smallest k error first, then the highest ARI:

kdb.k_accuracy(summary)
#          runs  mean_abs_k_error  exact_rate  mean_ARI
# method
# PRECAST     1               2.0         0.0    0.2615
# DeepST      1               3.0         0.0    0.5416
# SpaGCN      1               3.0         0.0    0.4487
# ...
Column Meaning runs successful runs with a reference annotation mean_abs_k_error mean of |k_error| over the runs exact_rate fraction of runs with exactly the reference k mean_ARI mean ARI over the runs

The table for all ten methods is in Benchmark the ten methods.

Failed runs, other datasets, other machines
  • Failed runs stay in summary with success = False, and k_accuracy leaves them out.
  • k_accuracy averages over every run of a method in summary. With several datasets or devices in one folder, filter first, for example summary[summary["dataset"] == "D3_151509_5k"].
  • A file without an annotation is not scored. Its runs keep k_estimated, and score_error says why (Your own data).
  • Runs made on another machine record the input file's path there. load_results(root, h5ad="data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad") scores them against your copy. For runs of several datasets, name a file for each: h5ad={"D3_151509_5k": "data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad", ...}.
  • load_results(root, reference_key="layer_guess") scores against another obs column, and score=False skips scoring and only collects the run records.
  • kdomainbench summarize --csv summary.csv prints both tables from the command line.

docs.title: The twelve metrics of the paper
docs.text:
kdb.evaluate scores a run in Python. kdb.metrics computes the twelve metrics of the paper with the paper's own code, so it needs the metric R packages (Installation) and kdb_py. Every spot needs a label from the run and an annotation in obs["clusters"], and the annotation needs at least two domains.

kdb.metrics("kdb_results/DR.SC/D3_151509_5k_cpu").round(4)
# metric
# ARI         0.2333
# spARI       0.2110
# NMI         0.4826
# FM          0.3780
# AMI         0.3980
# Purity      0.7048
# HOM         0.6078
# COM         0.4001
# PAS         0.1331
# CHAOS       0.0610
# LISI        1.4928
# SCS       380.8270

The result is saved as metric.csv in the run folder. A later call reads it back, and kdb.load_results then adds the ten other metrics as columns. From the shell, kdomainbench metrics kdb_results/ computes them for every finished run that has none yet.

Metric What it measures Better Computed with ARI adjusted Rand index between the labels and the annotation higher clevr spARI an ARI that also weighs how far apart the disagreeing spots lie higher spARI NMI normalized mutual information, with the arithmetic mean of the two entropies as the norm higher aricode FM Fowlkes–Mallows index higher clevr AMI adjusted mutual information higher aricode Purity share of spots in the most common annotated domain of their label higher ClusterR HOM homogeneity: each label holds spots of one annotated domain higher clevr COM completeness: each annotated domain falls under one label higher clevr PAS share of spots with another label than most of their 10 nearest spots lower SpatialPCA CHAOS mean distance from a spot to the nearest spot with the same label lower SpatialPCA LISI median local inverse Simpson index of the labels around a spot. 1 means one label lower lisi SCS spatial coherence score: how far the label pairs of neighboring spots are from 1,000 random shuffles, as an absolute Z-score higher PASTE's code

The first eight compare the labels with the reference annotation. The last four use only the labels and the spot coordinates. Citation lists the publications behind spARI and the last four.

docs.title: Plot the metrics
docs.text:
kdb.pl.plot_metrics draws the metrics of every run in a summary table, laid out as Fig. 2f of the paper:

summary = kdb.load_results("kdb_results")     # read again, now with the metrics
ax = kdb.pl.plot_metrics(summary)
ax.figure.savefig("metrics.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")

  • Rows and columns. One row per method and one column per metric. The paper sorts the metrics into four groups: concordance with the annotation, completeness, spatial coherence and stability.
  • Bar. The value of the metric, on the axis below its column. The left tick of an axis is 0, and a negative value is drawn to the left of it.
  • Fill. The rank of the method among the methods for that metric. The darkest bar is the best one, which is the lowest value where the arrow points down (LISI, PAS and CHAOS).
  • n/a. No value, such as the SCS of a run with one domain. This figure has none.

The figure shows the ten runs of Benchmark the ten methods. A method whose runs have no metric.csv has only its ARI and NMI bars, and with several runs per method a bar is their mean and a whisker their standard deviation.

Where the code comes from
  • The code is metrics.R and scs.py in src/kdomainbench/metric_scripts/, unchanged copies of the scripts that scored the paper's benchmark. A test fails when either file changes.
  • The file also needs obs["pixel_row"], obs["pixel_col"] and obsm["spatial"]. metrics.R reads the barcodes as numbers when they look like numbers, and then finds no match. Visium barcodes such as AAACAAGTATCTCCCA-1 are not affected.
  • SCS runs in kdb_py because PASTE's code needs pandas below 3. With pandas 3 it returns no value, which kdb.metrics reports as an error.
  • A run with one domain has no SCS, because every shuffle of one label is the same labeling. The paper's results leave it empty too.
  • A failed call raises kdb.MetricsFailed. The output of the metric code is in metric.log in the run folder.
  • metric.csv is read back as it is. After the annotation changes, call kdb.metrics(run, recompute=True).
