docs.title: Run a method
docs.text:
kdb.run runs one method on one .h5ad file in the environment the method needs, waits for it, and returns one domain label per spot.

Summary

import kdomainbench as kdb
h5ad = "data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad"

clusters = kdb.run("SpaGCN", h5ad, kmax=30, device="cpu")
results  = kdb.run_all(h5ad, kmax=30)      # all ten

docs.title: Run one method
docs.text:
clusters = kdb.run("SpaGCN", h5ad, kmax=30, device="cpu")

The method name is case-insensitive, and aliases such as drsc work. kmax is the largest k the method may consider (for BNPSpace, the k it starts from). The reference entry lists every argument and its default.

While the method runs, its output is printed. The lines that start with [kdomainbench] come from kDomainBench:

[kdomainbench] note: SpaGCN selects k by itself, so kmax=30 is not used.
[kdomainbench] SpaGCN on CPU -> /path/to/kdb_results/SpaGCN/D3_151509_5k_cpu
...

The outputs on this page are those of the paper's benchmark run of SpaGCN on sample 151509.

docs.title: What kdb.run returns
docs.text:
A DataFrame indexed by spot_id with one cluster column:

clusters.head(3)
#                      cluster
# spot_id
# AAACAAGTATCTCCCA-1.2       2
# AAACAATCTACTAGCA-1.2       1
# AAACACCAATAACTGC-1.2       0
clusters["cluster"].value_counts().sort_index()
# 0    1556
# 1    1513
# 2    1288
# 3     429

The number of distinct labels is the method's estimated k (here 4).

docs.title: The run folder
docs.text:
Each run writes to <out_root>/<method>/<dataset>_<device>, by default under kdb_results/. <dataset> is the name of the input file without .h5ad:

kdb_results/SpaGCN/D3_151509_5k_cpu/
├── cluster_results.csv   # spot_id,cluster
├── run.log               # everything the method printed
├── packages.txt          # the packages of the method's environment
└── run_info.json         # the record of the run: what ran, and with which settings
run_info.json
{
  "method": "SpaGCN",
  "dataset": "D3_151509_5k",
  "h5ad": "/path/to/kDomainBench/data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad",
  "kmax": 30,
  "device_requested": "cpu",
  "device_used": "cpu",
  "gpu_id": null,
  "returncode": 0,
  "kdomainbench": "0.1.0",
  "command": ["/path/to/envs/kdb_py/bin/python", "/path/to/methods/run_spagcn.py",
              "--data_path", "/path/to/kDomainBench/data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad",
              "--save_path", "/path/to/kdb_results/SpaGCN/D3_151509_5k_cpu/cluster_results.csv"],
  "env": {"KDB_METHODS_DIR": "/path/to/kdomainbench/methods", "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES": ""},
  "success": true,
  "n_spots": 4786,
  "k_estimated": 4
}

The record holds more fields than shown here. The Notes of kdb.run explain each one. kdb.read_clusters("kdb_results/SpaGCN/D3_151509_5k_cpu") reads the labels back later.

A second run into the same folder replaces the first. To keep both, give the second one another out_root, for example kdb.run("DR.SC", h5ad, out_root="kdb_results_kmax20", kmax=20).

When a method fails

kdb.run raises kdb.MethodFailed. The message names the log and ends with its last lines:

MethodFailed: BayesSpace failed (exit 1), see /path/to/kdb_results/BayesSpace/D3_151509_5k_cpu/run.log
...

run_info.json records the run with "success": false, also when the run was killed, for example by a time limit. Troubleshooting lists the common errors.

docs.title: Run several methods
docs.text:
results = kdb.run_all(h5ad, kmax=30, device="cpu")
# {'PRECAST': <clusters>, 'SC.MEB': <clusters>, ...}
results = kdb.run_all(h5ad, methods=["DR.SC", "SC.MEB"])

The methods run one after another, each into its own run folder under the same out_root. run_all reports a method that fails, or whose environment is missing, goes on with the next one, and ends with one warning that names every method that did not finish.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
The methods were written for 10x Visium data. The .h5ad file needs:

Field Used by Content X all raw counts (sparse or dense) obs_names all unique spot barcodes. They become spot_id var_names all gene names obs["array_row"], obs["array_col"] PRECAST, SC.MEB, BayesSpace, BNPSpace, DR.SC, iSC.MEB integer Visium grid coordinates obs["pixel_row"], obs["pixel_col"] SpaGCN pixel coordinates obsm["spatial"] CellCharter, DeepST, SpatialDE2, plotting 2-D coordinates (spots × 2) obs["clusters"] scoring only (optional) reference annotation: the annotated domain of each spot

Your own data builds such a file from a Space Ranger folder.

Other platforms than Visium

The R scripts build Visium (hexagonal) neighbor graphs, and CellCharter uses a 6-neighbor grid. For ST, Slide-seq or imaging data, change the platform argument in the R scripts under src/kdomainbench/methods/, or the CellCharter spatial_neighbors call.

docs.title: GPU or CPU?
docs.text:
CellCharter, DeepST and SpatialDE2 can run on a GPU. The examples below write to their own out_root, so that Evaluate a run compares the CPU runs only:

kdb.run("CellCharter", h5ad, kmax=30, device="gpu", out_root="kdb_results_gpu")
# [kdomainbench] CellCharter on GPU (GPU 0) -> /path/to/kdb_results_gpu/CellCharter/D3_151509_5k_gpu

gpu_id picks the GPU (reference entry), and kdomainbench check --gpu tells you beforehand whether a GPU is visible.

The other seven methods have no GPU code. With device="gpu" they still run, on the CPU, and warn:

kdb.run("PRECAST", h5ad, kmax=30, device="gpu", out_root="kdb_results_gpu")
# UserWarning: PRECAST has no GPU implementation. It runs on the CPU.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
terminal
kdomainbench run -m SpaGCN -i data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad -k 30 -d cpu
kdomainbench run -m CellCharter DeepST -i data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad -d gpu --gpu-id 0 -o kdb_results_gpu
kdomainbench run -m all -i data/D3_151509_5k.h5ad -d cpu

The runs go to the same folders as from Python, and -o DIR replaces kdb_results (Command line).
